title: For q>p and noncoalescing positive-real-part paired parameters satisfying (1.13), the complex-field Barnes–Ismagilov integral equals the finite quadratic hypergeometric expression Sigma_+^C
author: Yury A. Neretin
source_title: Barnes-Ismagilov Integrals and Hypergeometric Functions of the Complex Field
difficulty_reason: The central obligation is to evaluate an integral with a simultaneous discrete Mellin index and continuous contour variable, whose paired Gamma poles must be matched across both indices. The proof derives their joint lattice parametrization, computes complex Gamma residues and reorganizes them into a finite sum of products of ordinary hypergeometric series with a convergence justification. This exceeds a routine single-variable residue exercise and does not merely apply the classical Meijer formula without the new discrete-index calculation.
source_version: Official SIGMA 16 (2020) article 072, DOI 10.3842/SIGMA.2020.072; journal PDF and native TeX acquired 2026-09-30, exact bytes pinned by SHA256

proof_review.method: Published author proof/core and local context fidelity screening
proof_review.note: The entire q>p author residue proof of Theorem 1.2 was read with the complex Gamma asymptotics, pole parametrization and Mellin–Barnes decomposition in Sections 2.1–2.3. The source explicitly reorganizes the integer-indexed residues by two independent nonnegative indices and factors them into two convergent ordinary hypergeometric series, justifying the interchange by absolute convergence and noting local uniformity where the coefficients are defined. The classical Meijer residue theorem is genuinely prior background; the complex-field double-index factorization is supplied. Select only q>p and coefficient-regular, noncoalescing parameters, not the right-pole analogous branch, unit-circle/balanced case, or subsequent meromorphic continuation.

statement_scope: Exactly the explicitly proved q>p branch of Theorem 1.2(a), at z in C^*, with q paired a parameters and p paired b parameters in Lambda_C (a-a prime and b-b prime integral), Re(a_alpha+a_alpha prime)>0 and Re(b_beta+b_beta prime)>0, and total sum of these real parts <p+q as (1.12)–(1.13). Restrict to the noncoalescing coefficient-regular locus where expression (1.18) is defined (in particular no integer differences a_alpha-a_j for alpha!=j); the equality is pG_q^C=Sigma_+^C of (1.18). No extension through singular coefficients or parameter analytic continuation is included.
editorial_warning: Editorial typography notice, separate from the author: Lemma 2.3(a) concludes “Im sigma<0” after proving a+a prime+sigma is nonpositive integral, whereas its statement and contour separation use Re sigma<0. The immediately preceding displayed equation fixes the intended half-plane; the original statement and proof remain unchanged. Native (1.8a) prints (-1)^(a-a) where (1.7) explicitly supplies the paired-parameter sign. These local slips are not replaced in the reproduced source.
